messages:
maria-nguyen: Heads-up — planning a maintenance window for AZ3 next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Work items: PDU swap on rack-14, BMC firmware update on cohort-c, and thermal threshold recalibration. Rolling across racks, aiming for no-hosted-impact but Dedicated pools might see short capacity dips.
kevin-tang: timeline noted. any perf tests in staging with the new BMC fw? last cycle added small p95 noise.
nash-patel: ran a short smoke + perf run last night on staging: fw 1.2.6 -> 1.2.8. p50/p95 for gen workloads ~unchanged, but observed nvme IO wait spikes during node reboot sequence (~30s) on 3/40 nodes. logging attached in test run.
jules-m: can you paste the reboot sequence? want to validate drain hooks are firing in the right order.
nash-patel: snippet: ```
# drain sequence
kubectl cordon node/gpu-az3-14-03
kubectl drain node/gpu-az3-14-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
systemctl stop redwood-inference.service
flash-bmc --update fw-1.2.8
reboot
```
samir-r: question: are we planning to pre-stage backfill capacity in EU/US to absorb Dedicated load? cost-wise that means spinning up extra spot and reserved capacity for ~2 hours. estimate ~ $450/hr if we hold 12 T4s + 6 A10g for headroom.
maria-nguyen: yes, plan is to pre-warm a cross-region backfill pool. ops-budget approved up to $1.2k for the window — prefer to stay under. If we hit >$900, fallback to canary-only for Dedicated.
kevin-tang: SLA impact: support wants an automated customer notification if any Dedicated instance sees >2min reduced throughput or failed rollouts. can we add a short playbook?
nash-patel: added a small runbook change in the thread: ```
- monitor: per-pool p50/p95, inflight requests
- alert: if Dedicated pool capacity < 90% for >120s
- action: autoscale from backfill pool + mute bulk deploys
- fallback: failover to compatible model-variant in hosted region
```
jules-m: preflight checklist for Thursday run? we should also run a thermal soak for 45m after reboots to verify thresholds.
maria-nguyen: preflight items: 1) perf bench on staging (done) 2) backfill pool up (30m before) 3) alerting hooks live (15m before) 4) notify customers via status page (1h before) 5) oncall pager assigned.
samir-r: will coordinate with billing to track incremental cost tags: tag compute with maintenance-window-1777771234 so finance can attribute.
kevin-tang: small ask for infra: add max-surge=0 for the nodegroup during drain to avoid new nodes coming up mid-firmware; we want stable cohort.
maria-nguyen: good call. also we'll stagger PDU swaps: swap half the rack PDUs, validate power sequencing, then finish. anticipate a ~6m outage per BMC flash+reboot but we'll do staggered so application traffic unaffected.
oncall-bot: scheduled: maintenance window created (1777771234) | oncall: @samir-r | notify: status.redwood.ai/incidents/1777771234 | reminder: 60m before.
kevin-tang: final Q — any dependent network config changes (eg eBPF QoS) during the window? don't want egress churn.
jules-m: no network config changes. only QoS sanity sweep post-maint to validate egress shaping still intact.
maria-nguyen: TL;DR: Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC, AZ3 rolling PDU+BMC+thermal validation. backfill pool pre-warmed, alerts/playbook in place, finance tagging, oncall assigned. I'll post a final status notice to #announcements 1h before. :white_check_mark:
